personaSeed: You are a developer in a hurry between meetings. You use keyboard shortcuts on instinct, you guess at URLs, and you abandon any flow that takes more than four clicks.

findings.summary: Adopting a repo that pnpm can't install is impossible and opaque: /Users/alexraymond/open-design failed three times in a row at 'pnpm install', each time labeled 'Harness malfunction — not a verdict' with no command output shown, no retry button on the failure page, and no way anywhere in the UI to view logs or adjust the install/boot commands before adoption. A second repo (mission-control) failed the same way but did include pnpm stderr ('packages field missing or empty'), so error detail is inconsistent between failures.

The adoption review sheet's final confirm action sits below roughly five screens of boot-recipe JSON and journey proposals with no sticky footer; a user in a hurry sees 'Correct it', 'Accept all' and per-journey toggles but has to scroll a very long page to find the button that actually creates the project. I only located it by blind-probing button names (it matched /adopt/i).

The dashboard fires a POST to /api/dashboard that returns HTTP 405 (Method Not Allowed) repeatedly (roughly every 30 seconds while sitting on pages), filling the console with 'Failed to load resource' errors; the first occurrence coincided with my first Adopt submission, which also reset the form silently with no visible error or toast text.

On the adopted project's Knowledge tab, the boot recipe panel (install 'pnpm install', dev 'pnpm dev', fixed port 5173, health marker '/@vite/client', rationale citing a 'Vite renderer + Electron main' layout) directly contradicts the repo's own project.md rendered just below it, which says boot.json boots a Next.js app in apps/web on an OS-assigned port with health marker 'Ligma'. A user reading the page cannot tell which description of 'how it runs' is true.

The happy path did work end to end once a pnpm-installable repo was used: adoption crawled the repo, produced a review sheet where I confirmed the inferred boot recipe (the one confirmation asked of me) and accepted 5 proposed user journeys, and created a project whose Verify tab lists those journeys ('PROPOSED BY CRAWL') and whose Knowledge tab holds the ready boot recipe plus a 'First UX audit (adoption crawl)' describing what the app currently does; failure pages explicitly stated nothing was written into the repo.
